publicationTitle: IEE Technical Guidelines 9:1997 Embedded Systems and the Year 2000 Problem: Guidance Notes
abstract: Embedded systems contain a computer or a computer-like device which is used to control the operation of plant, machinery and equipment. They have been very useful and commercially successful.

publicationTitle: IEE Technical Guidelines 9:1997 Embedded Systems and the Year 2000 Problem: Guidance Notes
abstract: The goal of the investigation phase of a Year 2000 programme is to determine priorities for taking action on systems, which may be products or form part of the production process or plant.

publicationTitle: IEE Technical Guidelines 9:1997 Embedded Systems and the Year 2000 Problem: Guidance Notes
IEE Technical Guidelines 9:1997 Embedded Systems and the Year 2000 Problem: Guidance Notes
abstract: This chapter is concerned with procedures and checks relevant to those embedded systems or elements of systems where it is not practical to modify the software, even if it can be examined, and where as a result the device or component may need to be replaced to achieve date-compliance. In these systems, however, dates as such may not be the practical problem: the real problem may be the inability of the device to maintain a sequence of operations.

publicationTitle: IEE Technical Guidelines 9:1997 Embedded Systems and the Year 2000 Problem: Guidance Notes
abstract: This chapter deals with testing for date-sensitivity and compliance, including the precautions which need to be taken to ensure that testing does not cause to damage to operational systems.

publicationTitle: IEE Technical Guidelines 9:1997 Embedded Systems and the Year 2000 Problem: Guidance Notes
abstract: The requirement to change date formats depends on the use wich is made of the data and also on whether the program and the system will function satisfactorily without changes. It may be for example that, after a system is in operation (and can be started and stopped as appropriate) in Year 2000, dates and times will cause no further poroblems, even though special steps have been needed with the rollover itself.

publicationTitle: IEE Technical Guidelines 9:1997 Embedded Systems and the Year 2000 Problem: Guidance Notes
abstract: Two distinct but not entirely separate aspects of law need to be considered with respect to Year 2000 problems. The first applies to all Year 2000 problems. It is concerned with the contractual relationships and obligations you may have with your suppliers, customers and employees. This is discussed below. The second aspect, which needs particular consideration in relation to embedded systems (but may also apply to systems where there is no directly controlled machinery), is your obligations under "protection" legislation (including regulations and EC directives) covering matters such as health and safety and consumer protection. This is discussed in Chapter 14.

articleTitle: Embedded Systems and the Year 2000 Problem Guidance Notes
publicationTitle: IEE Technical Guidelines 9:1997 Embedded Systems and the Year 2000 Problem: Guidance Notes
IEE Technical Guidelines 9:1997 Embedded Systems and the Year 2000 Problem: Guidance Notes
abstract: Any Year 2000 programme requires actions to be initiated and planned. This chapter discusses why such a programme is needed and considers factors which may directly or indirectly impinge upon it. The matters which need to be considered in planning are indicated. The impact on staff throughout the organisation is considered, and, because appropriate staff may not be available, suggestions are made about what needs to be considered when choosing consultants. The chapter closes with an action plan which summarises the actions to be taken and which may serve as a checklist for smaller companies.

publicationTitle: IEE Technical Guidelines 9:1997 Embedded Systems and the Year 2000 Problem: Guidance Notes
abstract: This chapter contains a number of definitions and categorisations of embedded systems, given for different people and purposes. There is also a list of applications.

publicationTitle: IEE Technical Guidelines 9:1997 Embedded Systems and the Year 2000 Problem: Guidance Notes
abstract: This chapter describes a procedure for managing a Year 2000 programme. The procedure is applicable to general computer systems, embedded systems and (with modification) to programmes which have a wider remit than date sensitivity. Systems and hardware checking and software checking are described in Chapters 7 and 8 respectively.

publicationTitle: IEE Technical Guidelines 9:1997 Embedded Systems and the Year 2000 Problem: Guidance Notes
abstract: This section deals with checks and tests for date-sensitivity and compliance in embedded systems in which it is possible to test and modify the software, and particularly to larger and more complex systems. Relevant technical knowledge will be needed to undertake the work suggested. A list of functions and characteristics intended to assist the identification of systems which may have date-problems is given in Section 5.4.3. Some of the advice is relevant to general investigations including hardware. Advice is given on possible remedial actions.

articleTitle: Actions Where Software Cannot be Modified
publicationTitle: IEE Technical Guidelines 9:1997 Embedded Systems and the Year 2000 Problem: Guidance Notes
abstract: This chapter deals with actions which may be taken in relation to components and devices which cannot be modified, where the cost of modification may not be justifiable, or to prepare for unexpected or unforeseeable failures, or where the failure and its causes lie outside the control of the company. It also considers possible general benefits from Year 2000 programs and the avoidance of temporary fixes.

publicationTitle: IEE Technical Guidelines 9:1997 Embedded Systems and the Year 2000 Problem: Guidance Notes
abstract: This chapter outlines what is believed to be the current position with regard to the legal liabilities of the designer and the supplier of systems. It was originally written in connection with publications on safety related systems and has been revised for the present document.

publicationTitle: IEE Technical Guidelines 9:1997 Embedded Systems and the Year 2000 Problem: Guidance Notes
abstract: Creating reports and the establishment of a system for the storage and retrieval of documents (including correspondence) serves the following purposes: (a) The conduct of the project (b) Management progress review (c) Provision to and availability of information for customers (d) Provision of evidence in relation to disputes (e) Satisfaction of statutory and regulatory requirements.
